title: GitHub Copilot Workspace just made junior devs obsolete

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: If GitHub Copilot Workspace removes the need for junior developers, what does that mean for the future of software engineering?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: It automates coding tasks, suggesting full functions and debugging, allowing experienced devs to focus on architecture and strategy.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: This risks devaluing entry-level roles, potentially displacing thousands and widening the gap between skilled and unskilled workers.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Builders are integrating Copilot with mentorship tools, pairing AI suggestions with human feedback to train new developers.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: In five years, we might see AI-assisted apprenticeships, where juniors learn through guided collaboration, not replacement.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The future isn’t replacement—it’s redefinition, where AI and humans co-create, each amplifying the other’s potential.

video_cue: A split-screen showing a junior developer working alongside an AI interface, with code suggestions and real-time feedback appearing on the screen.
